case_title: Dauvaram Nirmalkar v. State of Chhattisgarh
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (brother); the deceased reportedly quarrelled with and abused the accused, and the deceased was addicted to alcohol
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 (charged and convicted at trial); IPC s.304 Part I (final conviction after applying Exception 1 to s.300); Evidence Act s.106 (burden) referred to
evidence_type: Circumstantial evidence (joint presence on the night, absence of any intruder); medical evidence (post-mortem); recovery evidence (pick-axe, blood-stained shirt, body discovered at the accused's residence); disclosure admissible under s.27
confession: Extra-judicial confession at police station on 26th September 2011. Held inadmissible under s.25; only the part leading to discovery of pick-axe and body was relied on under s.27
mitigating_circumstances: Prolonged alcohol-fuelled abuse and threats by the victim; on the night, victim allegedly threatened to kill the accused; sudden loss of self-control
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.302 for murder; life imprisonment, fine Rs.1,000, default simple imprisonment for six months
high_court_outcome: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 400 of 2013) decided by judgment dated 25.02.2019; conviction under s.302 upheld (Supreme Court agreed with High Court on involvement of the accused)
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s.304 Part I
neutral_facts: The victim, the accused's brother, died from coma caused by shock after multiple fractures to the skull, including the left temporal, frontal, parietal and left occipital regions with a deep lesion, and a lacerated wound on the chin, as recorded in the post-mortem report proved by a senior medical officer. The accused and the victim lived in separate rooms in the same house. Several witnesses, including relatives and a neighbour, testified that the victim was addicted to alcohol, was abusive and ill-tempered, and quarrelled with the accused. Two nieces who were present in the house at the time of the incident gave evidence, and neither reported any intruder or third person that night. It was the prosecution's case that the victim had consumed alcohol and told the accused to leave the house, failing which he would kill the accused. The accused had also tried to kill himself by holding live electrical wires and suffered burns to the hands. On 26th September 2011 the accused went to a police station and confessed. Following the accused's disclosure, a pick-axe was recovered from a wooden box in the residence; the pick-axe and the shirt worn during the incident were found stained with blood. The victim's body was discovered in the house where the accused resided.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from coma due to shock; multiple skull fractures (left temporal, frontal, parietal, left occipital) with deep lesion; lacerated wound on chin
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.302); 1 finally upheld (converted to s.304 Part I)
premeditation_planning: No premeditation or planning found; the Court held the killing followed sudden loss of self-control
motive: Sudden and grave provocation from the victim's prolonged alcohol-fuelled abuse and threats, culminating in the night's threat to kill the accused (accepted by the Court for Exception 1)
key_evidence_accepted: Joint presence of accused and victim on the night; no intruder evidence; post-mortem findings; s.27 disclosure leading to pick-axe, blood-stained shirt and body; evidence of victim's alcohol addiction and abuse from PW-3, PW-4, PW-8, PW-9, PW-10
witness_credibility: Public witnesses declared hostile but Court relied on their unison deposition on separate rooms and the victim's alcohol addiction; PW-10 did not admit making the statement attributed to her by PW-9; no third-party suggestion put to witnesses
post_offence_conduct: Went to police station on 26th September 2011 and confessed; disclosure led to recovery of pick-axe and discovery of the body
custody_duration: Over 10 years; in custody since 27 September 2011 (as stated by the Supreme Court)
trial_duration: offence: not given; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25.02.2019; Supreme Court: 02.08.2022
legal_representation: Appellant: Harinder Mohan Singh (Adv.). Respondent (State of Chhattisgarh): Sumeer Sodhi and Dhruv Wadhwa (Advs.)
investigation_status: Post-mortem conducted and proved; accused's disclosure led to recovery of pick-axe and body; trial completed with conviction. Charge sheet filing not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment, fine Rs.1,000. High Court (Criminal Appeal No. 400 of 2013, 25.02.2019): conviction upheld. Supreme Court: partly allowed; conviction converted to s.304 Part I; sentence modified to period undergone
prosecution_argument: Not stated in the judgment as separate submissions; the prosecution relied on the victim's alcohol addiction and abusive conduct to show motive
defence_argument: Not stated in the judgment as Supreme Court submissions; at trial the accused's s.313 statement suggested a third person killed the victim, which was rejected
legal_principle_applied: Exception 1 to s.300 IPC: grave and sudden provocation, loss of self-control, reasonable man test, cumulative provocation with a verifiable final act, and absence of premeditation
precedent_relied_upon: Aghnoo Nagesia v. State of Bihar [1966] 1 SCR 134; K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra [1962] 1 Suppl. SCR 567; Budhi Singh v. State of Himachal Pradesh (2012) 13 SCC 663; Rampal Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2012) 8 SCC 289 (referred to); R v. Duffy (1949) 1 All E.R. 932 (quoted)
sentencing_rationale: Appellant had already been incarcerated for over 10 years, so the sentence of imprisonment was modified to the period already undergone
judicial_mitigating_factors: Sudden and grave provocation from victim's alcohol-fuelled abuse and threats; sudden loss of self-control; the accused's own suicide attempt as evidence of temporary loss of control
other_sentence_order: Appellant to pay fine of Rs.1,000 (default six months simple imprisonment); to be released forthwith on payment if not required in any other case
